title: A slow install is undiagnosable from app.log - the download path logs no rate, no free space and no response headers
description: A beta user on fiber saw installs crawl at 20-40 KB/s against a ~50 MB/s line, and the two app.log captures he sent carry no byte-rate, no free-space figure and no response header - every rate had to be derived by differencing "resuming X from N GB" offsets against timestamps, which only works when a stall fires and a slow-but-alive stream never stalls. Adds three log lines: free space on the models + userData volumes, a latched slow-stream WARN carrying rate/host/resolved IP/cf-ray POP, and a timed write probe to the models root on that trigger. Does NOT change download behaviour, does NOT touch the concurrency cap (rejected on the record, routes/downloadManager.js:628) and does NOT rework the transport (that is MPI-657 Not-in-scope, which this card feeds). Evidence: C:/AI/Mpi/_private/cubric-download-telemetry/. Two sibling findings are recorded in brief.md and are NOT carded yet.
